about.title: Oildale Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member because of someone else's carelessness reshapes everything, and Oildale families often face this alongside funeral arrangements, missed work, and unanswered questions about what happened on a local road or job site. California law gives certain surviving family members, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, the right to bring a civil wrongful death action separate from any criminal proceeding tied to the incident. That claim can address funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their companionship and guidance. Because Oildale sits within Kern County's court system, cases here move through local procedures that an attorney familiar with the area can help you navigate. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect Oildale families with an independent attorney who can review the circumstances and explain your options at no upfront cost, so you can focus on your family during a difficult time.

whyChoose.title: Why Oildale Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death claim, prioritizing spouses, domestic partners, and children before other dependents or heirs. An attorney can quickly clarify where your family stands and what that means for your claim.

items.title: Awareness of the Filing Deadline
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window. Getting connected early helps preserve your family's ability to act within these deadlines.

items.title: Recognizing What Losses Count
items.desc: Beyond funeral and burial expenses, California law allows recovery for lost financial support and for the loss of love, companionship, and guidance your loved one provided. An attorney can help document these losses accurately for your family's claim.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may qualify under California law. An independent attorney can review your family's specific situation and confirm who has standing.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim after losing someone in Oildale?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If a government entity, such as a public road authority in Kern County, may be involved, the deadline to act is much shorter. Speaking with an attorney soon after the loss helps protect your family's rights.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action focused on compensating your family, even if criminal charges are filed against the responsible party. The two cases proceed independently and have different standards and outcomes. An attorney can explain how each process may affect your family's claim.

items.question: What costs are involved in speaking with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: LawProactive is a free service that connects Oildale families with an independent attorney, and there's no cost to have your situation reviewed. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if your family recovers compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after that initial conversation.
